newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania and Hungary vow to fight extremists.
newsitem.headline: Romania and Hungary vow to fight extremists.

text.p: The presidents of Romania and Hungary vowed on Tuesday to prevent nationalist extremists from undermining a historic reconciliation between the two countries, once uneasy neighbours.

"Let us not allow, let us together prevent anyone, however loud-mouthed, to obstruct good will and the achievement of our primary interests," Hungarian president Arpad Goncz told thousands of residents of the Transylvanian city of Tirgu Mures at the end of his three-day visit to Romania.

Goncz's visit to Romania, the first by a Hungarian head of state for 70 years, is seen as a major step towards reconciliation between the two states, until recently entangled in a tug-of-war over borders and the rights of Romania's 1.6 million ethnic Hungarians.
Six people were killed in 1990 in inter-ethnic clashes in Tirgu Mures, which has a large ethnic Hungarian population.
Last year the two countries signed a treaty intended to end disputes and pave the way for their ambitious plans to win early entry into NATO and the European Union.
"We will not allow any extremist minority in Romania or Hungary to speak on behalf of our peoples," said Romanian President Emil Constantinescu, who accompanied Goncz in his tour.

His remarks were an apparent reference to the nationalist mayor of the Transylvanian city of Cluj, who became famous for his anti-Hungarian stand. Gheorghe Funar curbed the minority's language rights and removed city street signs with Hungarian names.
Hundreds of Romanian nationalists in Cluj answered Funar's calls and staged a rally on Monday to protest against Goncz's visit.
Earlier on Tuesday, Goncz and Constantinescu visited Cluj but were given a warm welcome by residents and no incidents were reported.
"I feel at home and among brothers," Goncz said in Cluj, fighting back tears.
Romania hopes to be invited to join NATO along with favourites Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic when the military alliance announces its first eastward expansion at a Madrid summit in July.
